content_units: Talent Show Plan for Ages 13–16

These 12 act ideas are designed to be fun, school-appropriate, low-cost, and realistic to rehearse in under 2 weeks. They avoid copyright-sensitive dependence by using original writing, public-domain material, body percussion, or royalty-free/self-made audio.
12 Low-Cost Performance Ideas
Act Idea   Format   3–5 Minute Concept   Budget Fit   Rehearsal Ease
1   Original Stand-Up Set   Solo   Student performs a clean, school-friendly comedy set about homework, group chats, cafeteria food, or school life.   $0–$10   Easy
2   Character Monologue   Solo   A funny or dramatic original monologue from the perspective of a lost backpack, alarm clock, or overworked student.   $0–$15   Easy
3   Spoken Word Poetry   Solo   Perform an original poem on friendship, pressure, identity, or dreams with strong voice and stage presence.   $0–$5   Easy
4   Speed Sketch Challenge   Solo   Artist creates a large live drawing in 3–4 minutes while explaining the idea or revealing a surprise image at the end.   $10–$25   Easy
5   Beatbox + Body Percussion   Solo   A rhythmic act using only voice, claps, snaps, stomps, and desk/table-safe tapping if allowed.   $0   Medium
6   Two-Person Comedy Scene   Duo   Short original skit with a clear setup and twist, such as student vs. strict calculator or a chaotic science fair pitch.   $0–$20   Easy
7   Cup Rhythm Routine   Duo   Perform a synchronized rhythm piece using plastic cups and table-safe percussion patterns.   $5–$15   Medium
8   Illusion Through Misdirection   Duo   Simple, safe “magic” act using cards, paper, rubber bands, and practiced presentation rather than expensive tricks.   $10–$25   Medium
9   News Desk Parody   Trio/Group   Students play anchors reporting absurd but school-safe “breaking news” like locker traffic or pencil shortages.   $0–$20   Easy
10   Freeze-Frame Improv   Group   Players act out a scene while one narrator changes the situation every 20–30 seconds for laughs.   $0   Easy
11   Stomp-Style Percussion   Group   Use buckets, pencils, rulers, and body percussion to build a high-energy rhythm performance.   $15–$40   Medium
12   Mini Musical Mash-Up Without Copyright Risk   Group   Perform an original short musical scene using student-written lyrics over body percussion or royalty-free backing.   $0–$30   Medium

Solo options
Option 1: Original Stand-Up Set   Lowest cost and very engaging if the student has confidence   Best for strong speakers

Fast Production Notes
Budget-friendly prop ideas
- Plastic cups, poster board, markers, cardboard desk sign, thrift-store tie/jacket, buckets, rulers, index cards
- Keep total shared prop spend under   $80   by reusing school supplies and borrowing costume basics
Rehearsal plan for under 2 weeks
- Days 1–2: choose act, script outline, assign roles
- Days 3–5: rough rehearsal and timing
- Days 6–9: tighten entrances, exits, pacing, and cues
- Days 10–12: costume/prop run-through
- Final 1–2 days: full timed rehearsal on performance space if possible
Copyright-safe choices
- Use original scripts, original lyrics, public-domain text, body percussion, or royalty-free audio
- Avoid performing popular songs, movie scenes, or viral audio unless the school has clear permission
Judges’ Talent Show Scoring Rubric
Use a simple 20-point rubric for quick judging:
Category   What to Look For   Points
Entertainment Value   Audience engagement, fun factor, memorable moments   1–5
Creativity   Original idea, clever concept, fresh presentation   1–5
Execution   Timing, coordination, confidence, clarity   1–5
Stage Presence   Voice, energy, expression, use of space   1–5
Quick scoring guide:
-   17–20  : Outstanding
-   13–16  : Strong performance
-   9–12  : Solid but could be tighter
-   4–8  : Needs more polish
